In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

re-irradiating malignant glioma is feasible and safe, provided that the cumulative dose is kept below a threshold of 75 Gy to the optic chiasma, 60 Gy to both optic nerves and below 70 Gy to brainstem.
the cumulative EUD is not a relevant parameter for the outcome of re-irradiated MG patients.
re-irradiated MGs may be treated with the same doses as primary irradiation without an additional risk of toxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EUD approach seems useful to estimate the cumulative dose to OARs in MG patients after primary and re-treatment.
re-irradiating patients for recurrent MG is safe and feasible.
EUD values are useful to estimate the cumulative dose to the OAR and that the EUD is superior to classical DVH parameters in terms of correlation with outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cumulative EUD values at the OAR are not correlated with survival outcome.
re-irradiating patients with MG is feasible and safe, and that cumulative EUD values are useful to predict the cumulative dose at OARs.
re-irradiated patients are not at increased risk of developing late radiation toxicity.
